solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Loose woman beginning to exasperate novelist

parts.note: a trollop is an old word for a promiscuous woman

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of exasperate is used

explanation.surface: A promiscuous woman starts to irritate a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope was a Victorian novelist, author of the Barsetshire novels.

clue.text: Illegal entrance for demolition of building

definitions.meaning: burglary by forcing a way into a home
read literally, the knocking apart of a dwelling

explanation.surface: A legal-sounding note that unlawful entry covers knocking a building down.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the legal name for burglary, and taken literally it describes smashing up a home.

clue.text: Old country prospers, I assume, with several outsiders banished

indicators.note: dropping several letters from each outer end of the phrase prospers, I assume leaves a run from inside it

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a nation thrives.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip PROS from the front and SSUME from the back of 'prospers, I assume' and the middle remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia is the former name of Iran, so it is a country of the past.

clue.text: Bull inflicted lacerations on us, we'd say

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to tear someone is to lacerate them, so this is 'tore us'

explanation.surface: A bull gored us, as we would put it.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus is the zodiac sign and constellation of the Bull.

clue.text: What schemes will be profitable? Maybe we toss a coin!

definitions.meaning: ventures that bring in lots of cash
people flipping coins literally set cash spinning

explanation.surface: Wondering which plans will pay, and deciding by flipping a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucrative ventures are called this, and coin tossers are literally people who spin cash.

clue.text: Little boy eats a vegetable

indicators.note: a name that eats something takes it inside, so a goes within the boy's name

parts.note: Ben is a short form of Benjamin, a boy's name

explanation.surface: A small child eats some greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Beans are pod-grown edible seeds eaten as vegetables.

clue.text: Poet conveying the sound of running water

indicators.note: says the name is pronounced like a word for a stream

parts.note: a brook is a small stream

explanation.surface: A poet whose verse evokes the babble of a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Brooke was an English poet of the First World War.

clue.text: Fuss socialist loved

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother
red is a common label for a left-winger

explanation.surface: A left-winger who made a fuss was much cherished.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to love them deeply, both past-tense verbs.

clue.text: Drinks imbibed by female sometimes

indicators.note: what is drunk by a phrase is held within it, so the letters sit inside female sometimes

explanation.surface: Beverages a woman occasionally drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ales are beers, so they are drinks.

clue.text: Officer ecstatic about new gear

indicators.note: one word placed around another, so the thrilled word surrounds the rest

parts.note: sent is old slang for thrilled or transported

indicators.note: a new version of gear has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An officer thrilled with his new kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ecstatic' seems to describe the officer but is old slang meaning thrilled; 'new' scrambles the kit word to RGEA, and 'about' wraps the slang word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned officer in the army or police.

clue.text: Abstains from supporting rude people

parts.note: to be for something is to back it
bears are gruff, ill-mannered people

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to back boorish folk.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to refrain from doing something, the same as abstaining.

clue.text: Farm animal in river in the morning

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
a.m. marks morning times

explanation.surface: A sheep found wading in a river at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A ram is a male sheep kept on farms.

clue.text: Not bad, thus can be repeated

indicators.note: the word for thus appears twice in a row

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: Saying it twice is merely acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something middling is not bad but not good either: mediocre.

clue.text: Son listening to pianist George

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
hearing is the act of listening

explanation.surface: A boy listens to a famous jazz pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: George Shearing was a blind British-born jazz pianist, composer of Lullaby of Birdland.

clue.text: Report of outcome in outdoor event

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is spoken not spelt

parts.note: fate is what ultimately happens, an outcome

explanation.surface: News of the result of an open-air gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is a British summer fair held outdoors, with stalls and games, often for charity.

clue.text: One politician shown to be damaged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
aired means broadcast or displayed

explanation.surface: A single MP is revealed as harmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaired means weakened or damaged.

clue.text: One of many keeping close together when there's a gale?

definitions.text: One of many keeping close together when there's a gale?

parts.words: One of many keeping close together when there's a gale?
parts.note: on a weather map, lines joining points of equal pressure crowd together when winds are strong

explanation.definitionFit: These pressure lines on weather charts bunch tightly in stormy conditions.

clue.text: Criticise a mother's summer hat

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
ma is mother, with the 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at their mum's sunhat.
explanation.definitionFit: A panama is a lightweight straw hat worn in warm weather.

clue.text: Withdraw, having returned to humbler position?

parts.note: back means returned, as in being back home
down means lower, brought low

explanation.surface: Retreating after being demoted on one's return.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb down from a position is to retreat or concede, an idiomatic sense of withdrawing.

clue.text: Perched and damaged tail

indicators.note: a damaged word is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird settles with a hurt tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Alit is a past tense of alight, to land or settle on something.

clue.text: Northern Queen meets old emperor

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A queen from the north encounters an ancient ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a Roman emperor of the first century.

clue.text: City girl returning after six

indicators.note: places the reversed name behind the numeral

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: going back, so the name is written backwards

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A town girl coming home after six o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital city of Austria.

clue.text: Soldier, one buried in site of battle

indicators.note: something buried is placed inside, so the numeral goes into the river's name

parts.note: the Marne, a French river, saw two major First World War battles
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A soldier, one laid to rest on a famous battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine is a soldier who serves with a navy.
